settings.headline: A different application. Two strengths.
settings.subhead: UK-formulated topical preparation gel, made for aesthetic appointments where the gel format suits the procedure better than a cream. Advanced and Professional — gel comes in two strengths.
settings.image_alt: Editorial still life of the Senseless gel range on a warm off-white background

settings.headline: Gel suits some procedures better than cream.
settings.body: Gel sits differently on the skin. Some practitioners prefer it for treated areas that need to stay exposed, or for procedures where cream isn't practical. Some clients prefer the texture. Gel comes in Advanced and Professional strengths — the same concentrations as the cream, in a format that suits a different kind of session. Choose by procedure, by practitioner preference, or by what feels right at the chair.

settings.headline: What comes next.
settings.body: Most aesthetic appointments end with a treated area that needs gentle handling. The Senseless Foaming Cleanser is built for the hours after. An antibacterial cleansing foam that respects what you just had done.
settings.image_alt: Editorial image of the Senseless Foaming Cleanser on a clean countertop

settings.question: Cream or gel — which should I choose?
settings.answer: Strength is the bigger decision. Format is the next one. Cream suits most appointments. Gel suits procedures where the cream format isn't practical, or where your practitioner prefers it. See the format guide.

settings.question: Is gel stronger than cream?
settings.answer: No. Strength is independent of format — an Advanced gel is the same concentration as an Advanced cream. Gel comes in Advanced and Professional (Clinical is cream only). Choose by format preference, not by an assumed strength difference.

settings.question: When do I apply gel?
settings.answer: Ahead of your appointment. Your practitioner is the best guide for the procedure you've booked.

settings.question: Can I use gel for tattoos?
settings.answer: Senseless is formulated for aesthetic procedures. For body art see our topical numbing for body art guide.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
